name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
hook: The Jazz Age's own novelist: five novels, one Zelda, and the most famous last line in American fiction.

facts.label: F. Scott Fitzgerald
facts.statement: F. Scott Fitzgerald was named for distant relative Francis Scott Key, grew up in St. Paul, Minnesota, and attended Princeton.

facts.label: This Side of Paradise
facts.statement: This Side of Paradise, his 1920 debut, made Princeton student Amory Blaine its hero and made Fitzgerald famous.

facts.label: The Great Gatsby
facts.statement: The Great Gatsby (1925) is his masterpiece; its last line about "boats against the current" inspired Eric Carmen, and Tom and Daisy meet at Louisville's Seelbach Hotel.

facts.label: Zelda Sayre
facts.statement: He met Zelda Sayre in Alabama in 1918 and married her; her flapper image shaped his heroines and his fiction.

facts.label: Tender Is the Night
facts.statement: Tender Is the Night (1934) was his last complete novel; its title comes from Keats's "Ode to a Nightingale".

facts.label: The Last Tycoon
facts.statement: The Last Tycoon, about a Hollywood producer, was unfinished when Fitzgerald died of a heart attack at 44 in 1940.

facts.label: the Jazz Age
facts.statement: Fitzgerald christened the 1920s the Jazz Age; his 1922 story collection Tales of the Jazz Age made the phrase stick.
